To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
flavor mediation delivers Natural SUSY.
Flavor Mediation is a novel and natural mechanism to generate the flavor structure of natural SUSY, and that it makes a number of predictions for the superpartners.

1) Flavor Mediation automatically delivers a natural spectrum, 2) the spectrum is unique, 3) it is compatible with gauge coupling unification, 4) the spectrum is testable at the LHC, 5) it is testable at flavor experiments, and 6) it is testably distinguishable from other models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the SM flavor structure can be used to solve the SUSY flavor problem. We find that it can.
the following question: can we build a natural SUSY model that is simultaneously predictive, gauge-coupling unified, and compatible with flavor physics? The answer is yes.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SM contains a hidden anomaly-free SU(2) flavor symmetry, and that SUSY breaking is mediated by this flavor symmetry.
Flavor Mediation is the first model of natural SUSY that does not introduce any new matter or gauge symmetries.
flavor mediation provides a simple and compelling realization of natural SUSY.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the flavor structure of the SM can be directly connected to the SUSY flavor structure.
flavor mediation delivers natural SUS
the flavor structure of the superpartners is determined by SM flavor, and this structure naturally explains the observed hierarchy of scalar masses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
flavor mediation can be used to construct models of Natural SUSY that are consistent with gauge coupling unification and LHC bounds, without the need for any new matter beyond the SM.
the SM flavor structure, which is a necessary part of the SM, can be used to explain the superpartner mass hierarchy and degeneracy of the first two generations.
flavor structure in SUSY models is not a random accident, but rather is intimately tied to the structure of the SM.
